cards.term: What animal is hunted on each of the three days?
cards.def: Day 1 deer (hinds and does), day 2 a wild boar, and day 3 a fox (Reynard).

cards.term: How many kisses does Gawain return each evening?
cards.def: One kiss on day 1, two kisses on day 2, and three kisses on day 3.

cards.term: What does Lady Bertilak say Gawain is free to do on the first morning?
cards.def: Lady Bertilak tells Gawain he is free to have her all, do with her what he will, and she will come just as he calls.

cards.term: Why does Lady Bertilak say Gawain cannot be his name?
cards.def: Because a man so courtly could never linger long with a lady without craving a kiss as politeness requires.

cards.term: What does Gawain refuse to tell Bertilak after the first kiss?
cards.def: By what wit he won the kiss, and when and where, because that wasn't their pact.

cards.term: What proverb does Bertilak use before the third day?
cards.def: "Think tomorrow third time throw best," after saying he has tested Gawain twice and found him truthful.

cards.term: What two gifts does Lady Bertilak offer on day 3 before Gawain accepts one?
cards.def: First a ring of rich red gold with a stunning stone, which Gawain refuses, then her green silk girdle.

cards.term: What does Lady Bertilak claim the green girdle can do?
cards.def: The body bound within it will be safe against anyone who seeks to strike him, and all the slyness on earth wouldn't see him slain.

cards.term: What promise about the girdle does Gawain make to Lady Bertilak?
cards.def: Gawain agrees not to whisper a word of the gift to her husband, so their words within those walls should stay.

cards.term: What does Gawain give Bertilak on the third evening, and what does he withhold?
cards.def: Gawain gives three kisses but withholds the green girdle he gained that day.

cards.term: What does Bertilak bring as his third-day winnings?
cards.def: Only a foul-stinking fox pelt, which he calls a miserable match for Gawain's three perfect kisses.

cards.term: How does Fitt III end for Gawain's schedule?
cards.def: Gawain says farewell, Bertilak assigns a servant to guide him to the Green Chapel, and Gawain lies thinking of the morning's destiny on New Year's Day.

cards.term: What time and place make up the setting of Fitt III?
cards.def: Fitt III takes place at Bertilak's castle, with Gawain in his bedroom and Bertilak hunting in the surrounding hills and woods, over three days that end on New Year's Eve.

cards.term: How does Gawain answer Lady Bertilak's hint on the second morning that he could take a kiss by force?
cards.def: When Lady Bertilak says that if a lady snubbed him, "a man like you has the means of his muscles," Gawain answers that "such heavy-handedness is frowned on in my homeland, and so is any gift not given with grace" (line 1499).

cards.term: What does Lady Bertilak ask Gawain to teach her on the second morning, and how does Gawain answer?
cards.def: Lady Bertilak asks Gawain for "some lessons in love," saying the chiefmost aspect of chivalry is "loyalty in love," but Gawain answers that explaining true love to a lady with more insight and skill than he or a hundred like him "would be somewhat presumptuous."

cards.term: How does Bertilak kill the boar on the second day?
cards.def: Bertilak dismounts, wades through the stream to the cornered boar, and when the boar bounds at him and both tumble into the white water, Bertilak knifes the boar's neck with his sword to the hilt, bursting its heart.

cards.term: What is Gawain dreaming of when Lady Bertilak wakes him on the third morning?
cards.def: Gawain mutters "like a mournful man" in dreams of how destiny might deal him a death blow when he grapples with the guardian of the Green Chapel and must suffer the strike of the axe without struggle.

cards.term: What bind does Lady Bertilak put Gawain in on the third morning?
cards.def: Lady Bertilak pushes Gawain to a limit where he must "allow her love or impolitely reject it," so Gawain must stay courteous and avoid uncouthness while also guarding his soul from sin and not being "counted a betrayer by the keeper of the castle" (line 1775).

cards.term: How does Gawain answer when Lady Bertilak asks whether he already loves another lady?
cards.def: Gawain tells Lady Bertilak, "You judge wrong, by Saint John... There is no other one nor will be for this while!", and Lady Bertilak calls those words "the worst of all" before kissing him.

cards.term: What gift does Lady Bertilak ask Gawain for on the third morning, and why does Gawain refuse?
cards.def: Lady Bertilak asks for "a glove at least" to remember him by, but Gawain says a glove would be a worthless token and that he is "here on an errand in an unknown land" with nothing finer to give.

cards.term: Why does Gawain refuse Lady Bertilak's ring?
cards.def: Gawain refuses the ring of rich red gold because "no tokens will I take at this time; I have nothing to give, so nothing will I gain," so Lady Bertilak offers her girdle instead as "a lesser thing to gain."

cards.term: Why does Gawain finally accept the green girdle after first refusing it?
cards.def: Gawain first says he will take "neither gold nor girdle" until his challenge is achieved, but after Lady Bertilak describes its power Gawain thinks "it might just be the jewel for the jeopardy he faced" and could save him from the strike at the Green Chapel (line 1856).

cards.term: Which saint does Bertilak swear by after the second exchange, and what does Bertilak say?
cards.def: "By Saint Giles," Bertilak tells Gawain after receiving two kisses for the boar, "You're now the best I know. By wagering this way your gains will grow and grow" (lines 1644-1647).

cards.term: How is Lady Bertilak dressed when she comes to Gawain's room on the third morning?
cards.def: Lady Bertilak rushes in wearing a flowing, fur-lined robe that reaches the floor, her head unhooded with gems entwined in her tresses "in clusters of twenty," her face and neck bare and her shoulders "bare to both back and breast," and she throws the window wide open (lines 1735-1743).
